title: Water can be ice, liquid, and vapor at ordinary surface conditions
summary: NASA says water is the only known substance that can naturally be a gas, a liquid, and a solid in the narrow range of temperatures and pressures at Earth's surface.
body: NASA's Earth Observatory water-cycle page, dated 1 October 2010, says water is the only known substance that can naturally exist as a gas, a liquid, and a solid within the relatively small range of air temperatures and pressures at Earth's surface. A caption on the same page says it is the only common substance that can do so, and that all three states can be present together, as in a winter geyser at Yellowstone. The page's inventory of how much water sits in oceans and ice is already on other cards and is not repeated. This card is the three-state claim.
